Campbell told Detroit media this week that he is expecting "a knockout, 60-minute brawl," so it sounds like he'll have his team fired up. Hopefully for the Jets, Glenn's return to face the team he used to coach will go better than Robert Saleh's did in Week 1.

Can the Jets exploit the Lions' banged-up secondary?

The Lions already knew they would be without two key members of their secondary with Brian Branch and Kerry Joseph starting the year on the PUP list. However, the crisis has deepened as Avonte Maddox was just placed on IR with a season-ending foot injury and Thomas Harper's status for Sunday is in doubt as he was in a walking boot earlier this week.

Glenn dealt with similar issues when he was the Lions' DC, and he proved adept at maintaining that unit with reserves and replacements. However, the 2026 Lions aren't finding this so easily, as they have given up the second-highest total in the NFL when it comes to both yards and points.

The Jets have only targeted Garrett Wilson 14 times in the first two games, so they may look to get him more involved this week. Then, if the Lions give extra attention to Wilson, Geno Smith will need to spread the ball around to some of the other weapons as he seeks mismatches.

Will New York be able to get the running game going?

In Week 1, the Jets looked like they were establishing an identity as a team that could run the ball efficiently to play ball control offense and dominate time of possession. Breece Hall rushed for over 100 yards and Braelon Allen also contributed well in the win over the Titans.

Surprisingly, they struggled to run the ball against a Packers team that was missing a few front seven starters. Hall picked up 14 on a second-half run, but otherwise he and Allen combined for just 22 rushing yards on 20 carries. Furthermore, Allen was stuffed on consecutive short-yardage plays near midfield with the score tied late in the game.

It's possible the Jets struggled to get any traction in the wet conditions and that their running game will show improvement this week against a Detroit run defense that ranks in the bottom five. They will need to, because getting into a shootout with the Lions is not advisable.

The Jets' special teams unit needs to bounce back

New York's special teams unit was one of its main strengths last season. Entering this year, the assumption was that they would build upon a strong first season with Chris Banjo at the helm, although there was a concern over the placekicker position.

So far, though, the kicker has been the least of the Jets' worries. They gave up over 200 return yards in Week 2, including a 63-yard punt that set up the field goal that sent the game into overtime.

In addition, the return game — which was so dominant last season — has provided very little with Kene Nwangwu injured. Isaiah Williams muffed two punts in the rain on Sunday.

How will the defense hold up against the Lions' dynamic offense?

Although their defense has been struggling, the Lions still have an outstanding offense, putting up 31 points in each of their first two games. You would imagine that the Jets, whose defense is currently No. 1 in the NFL based on yardage allowed, will need to keep them below that if New York is to have a shot at winning.

This will easily be their toughest test of the season so far, though. Jared Goff leads the league in touchdown passes and hasn't thrown an interception yet, while Amon-Ra St. Brown leads the league in receptions and touchdown catches.

Although David Montgomery is now in Houston, the Lions' running game also poses a threat. Jahmyr Gibbs has racked up 299 yards from scrimmage in the first two games, averaging 104 rushing yards per contest. This will test a Jets run defense that will be without one of their better run stoppers following the injury to David Onyemata.

item.title: Patriots vs. Jaguars weather forecast for NFL Week 3
item.description: An up-to-date weather forecast for the Sunday game.
item.content:encoded:
The New England Patriots have not played in 80-plus degrees since a game in Miami last September. That streak will come to an end on Sunday: their Week 3 road game against the Jacksonville Jaguars is projected to kick off at around 83°F.

According to NFL Weather, temperatures will climb to 85°F during the game while there is a slight chance of rain showers in the second half. Humidity, however, is not expected to exceed 30%. There will be wind gusts of up to 11 mph with the real-feel temperature hovering around 82-83°F all day.

For the Patriots, this marks a change compared to their first two games of the season. Both their season-opening loss in Seattle and their win over the Steelers in Foxborough last Sunday were played in comparatively moderate temperatures of 74°F and 63°F at kickoff, respectively.

Despite the increased heat, the forecast is still relatively favorable from a New England perspective. Jacksonville’s first opponent this season, after all, had to play in 90-degree weather with humidity in the 60s; the visiting Browns lost that game 34-10.

The Patriots leaving Florida with a different result in hand starts with preparing for the heat both mentally and physically.

“Have to be hydrated. Get an IV,” defensive tackle Milton Williams said on Thursday. “I’m going to put a hoodie on now for practice. … I try to make myself get accustomed to the heat a little bit more, but I feel like if you’re hydrated, you should be all right.”

Kickoff between the Patriots and Jaguars is scheduled for Sunday, Sept. 27 at 1 p.m. ET.

item.title: 3 Titans who need to come up big vs. Giants in Week 3
item.description: Identifying three Tennessee Titans players who could carry the team to victory vs. the Giants in Week 3.
item.content:encoded:
The Tennessee Titans have a winnable game versus the New York Giants in Week 3. The Titans played a competitive game against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 2. Meanwhile the Giants lost several starters to injury, including quarterback Jaxson Dart.

We’ve identified three Titans who could lead Tennessee to victory in Week 3.

WR Carnell Tate

Rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate has produced just seven receptions for 65 yards through two games. The fourth overall pick has started slower than anyone anticipated. Both Cam Ward and Tate have been responsible for missed opportunities.

The Giants’ secondary was torched by Davante Adams on MNF. Tate and the Titans’ passing attack should have opportunities to generate explosive plays on Sunday. It’s time for the rookie wideout to have his breakout game.

RB Tony Pollard

Tony Pollard ran the football rather effectively versus the Eagles in Week 2. He rushed for 64 yards via 14 carries, averaging 4.6 yards per attempt. He could have scored a touchdown if Ward didn’t scramble for two scores. Pollard is averaging 4.7 yards per carry.

The Titans’ offensive line has been better than expected or advertised. With Jaxson Dart missing Week 3, hopefully the Titans will control the football for longer as they currently rank 32nd in time of possession. Pollard could have a big day.

DT Jeffery Simmons

Superstar defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons was dominant versus the Eagles in Week 2. He currently leads the NFL in pressures. He’s playing like the Pro Bowl-caliber player he is in Robert Saleh’s new system.

The Giants have a rookie guard in Francis Mauigoa and a struggling center in John-Michael Schmitz. With Jameis Winston at quarterback, Simmons is definitely capable of forcing him into a mistake or two. He should be his usual reliable self.

item.title: Houston Texans Prediction at Colts Week Three
item.description: Giving you my *unbiased* opinions of the Texans-Colts Week Three matchup presented by Fanduel
item.content:encoded:
The Texans unfortunately enter familiar territory. For the second straight year and third time in the DeMeco Ryans era, the Texans are 0-2 out of the gate. They face their AFC South rivals the Indianapolis Colts (0-2), who’ve also tripped coming out of the gate. Both teams are exceptionally desperate for a win, and neither are off to the start they hoped after losing two games to perennial favorites in the AFC. The Colts lost two high scoring affairs to the Baltimore Ravens and Kansas City Chiefs and are looking to right the ship against the Houston Texan.

FanDuel’s odds currently favor the Texans by 1.5 points. Those odds are much lower than Houston fans would have hoped for and are indicative of the poor start the Texans have put together on both sides of the ball. 

Jonathan Taylor powers the Colts’ offense with 190 yards through two games. I predict he will have another productive and efficient day given the Texans difficulties stopping the run. No Henry To’oTo’o or Kayden McDonald means the Texans are vulnerable up the middle of the defense.

QB Daniel Jones has been thoroughly mediocre in his return from Achilles injury suffered last season. He has thrown two touchdowns and two interceptions. He has struggled to sustain drives and has not looked efficient in the red zone. 

Newly minted $114M man Alec Pierce has landed on Injured Reserve. He crushed the Texans last year and racked up 210 yards and three touchdowns in two games. His absence will be an immense blessing for a Texans defense surely in need of a reprieve and get-right game. 

As for the Texans’ offense, they quickly shifted away from the run against the Bengals, opting to throw the ball a career high 55 times for C.J. Stroud. This was ineffective and certainly not the game script from Offensive Coordinator Nick Caley. Expect Houston to commit, heavily to the run game and incorporate the screen game to break up the issues they’ve faced on offense. 

PREDICTION: Colts 24, Texans 17

The Texans offense have yet to put it together. Without WR Nico Collins in the line up there is no indication of their ability to score points. Plus, the Texans’ defense has been unusually porous to start the 2026 season, not to mention unable to convert any turnovers. 

Houston has to find a way to get WR Kayshon Boutte incorporated into the offense. Boutte leads the league in go-routes, but that’s simply not enough for him to positively impact this offense. Slants and screens are two easy options for the wide receiver to take more ownership of the air attack and help move the ball down the field. 

What separates these two teams is the Colts’ run game. Jonathan Taylor is the most effective weapon for either offense and will allow the Colts to control the tempo. Houston has yet to counter a strong rushing attack. QB Daniel Jones is fairly immobile, which is ideal for the Texans pass rush. In Week One, Bills QB Josh Allen detonated the Texans pass rush duo with his scrambling ability. Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter won’t have to worry about that with Jones, who has already been sacked twice this season. 

I predict Tyler Warren to have a very productive game against the Texans defense. He leads their team with nine receptions, but only 39 yards. Houston gave up play after play to Buffalo’s tight end Dalton Kincaid. Expect Jones to find Warren early and often on play action plays to decrease the pressure on the run game. 

The Colts late addition of Keenan Allen has paid dividends as his seven receptions is third on the team behind Josh Downs and Tyler Warren. He is facing a potential three-game suspension due to driving over the legal limit in Indianapolis earlier this month. If he plays he should be the focal point of CB Kamari Lassiter, who is desperately in need of a good game. The Texans have not let Lassiter and Derek Stingley Jr. follow specific receivers, which has led to ill-advised mismatches in the secondary. The Colts game presents an opportunity for Stingley Jr. to follow the faster Downs and Lassiter to pursue Allen. 

One player on the Texans offense to watch for is Jaylin Noel. He was featured more often this game than in previous contests, mostly out of desperation, but it’s a good sign of his growth and incorporation in Houston’s plans. Fans saw Dalton Schultz shine in a big role last week, which should most certainly be the case again if Nico Collins is sidelined with a hamstring injury again. 

Going 0-3 again is not ideal. The criticism and disgruntled emotions will be at an all-time high under the Ryans era. This team was supposed to be better than the last across the board and haven’t shown any progression on any of the fronts they addressed this offseason. The offensive line can’t pass protect or move the ball. The run game is putrid. Whoever plays safety next to Calen Bullock forgets how to play football (C.J. Gardner Johnson, Reed Blankenship). Will it be different this game and can the Texans right the ship earlier than last year? We’ll find out on Sunday.

item.title: 5 things to watch as Giants face Titans in Week 3 of 2026 NFL season
item.description: Here are the main storylines to watch as the shorthanded Giants look to bounce back in Week 3 against the Titans…
item.content:encoded:
The Giants are regrouping following Monday night's disappointing 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. 

The loss of QB Jaxson Dart for the remainder of the regular season was compounded by further injuries to key starters on both sides of the ball. 

Can Sunday's clash against the 0-2 Titans be a "get right" game for New York?

Here are the storylines to watch as Big Blue looks to bounce back…

Jameis Winston takes the reins

Dart's devastating injury has the potential to derail a promising first season for John Harbaugh as Giants head coach. However, at least New York has one of the NFL's more experienced backups in Winston.

Unfortunately, when Winston was called upon against the Rams, he responded poorly. 

The veteran backup struggled from the start, completing just one of his first six passes for one total yard. He ended up completing just 11 of 27 passes for 111 yards and threw a costly red zone pick with the Giants set up to cut into the deficit heading into halftime. 

Winston has had plenty of success in his career, but he's always been inconsistent. With a good team around him, he's shown he can win games, and optimism will pick up if he can defeat the Titans in a very winnable game.

Familiar faces look to step up against their old team

After being fired as the Giants' head coach midseason last year, Brian Daboll landed on Tennessee's staff as their new offensive coordinator, and he may be looking for a measure of revenge on Sunday.

A handful of players Daboll coached with the Giants now play key roles for the Titans, and they should be motivated to perform well on Sunday, too. That includes WR Wan'Dale Robinson, who will be looking for a breakout game after being held to just 47 yards and six catches so far this season.

The other former Giants in key roles are starting C Austin Schlottmann, CB Cor'Dale Flott and TE Daniel Bellinger, although Flott missed the last game due to injury and Bellinger is off to a slow start. 

Can Malik Nabers get going?

The Giants must have breathed a sigh of relief when Nabers returned to the game against the Rams after briefly departing in significant pain due to a shoulder injury.

However, he was completely ineffective during the game, ending up with just one catch for one yard.

This could be attributed to the fact that he's still not completely confident playing on his surgically repaired knee, but he seemed to be over that in Week 1, bringing in six passes for 69 yards in the win over Dallas.

With Winston known as a quarterback who is not afraid to take risks and air it out air it out, Nabers might actually enjoy playing with him, and the pair could quickly establish chemistry.

Watch out for Jeffery Simmons

The Titans' biggest weapon is Simmons, who is regarded as one of the best defensive linemen in the league.

Simmons racked up a whopping 11 sacks last season and is a force against the run, so he'll provide a major challenge for John Michael Schmitz, Jon Runyan, Jr. and the rookie Francis Mauigoa.

In this regard, facing star Rams DT Aaron Donald in Week 2 might have been useful in preparing New York for this challenge.

The Giants need more from their pass rush

New York's pass rush was one of their greatest strengths over the past few seasons, but they have gotten off to a slow start in Harbaugh's 3-4 system.

Abdul Carter broke through with a sack late in Monday night's game, but it was the only sack the Giants have registered so far this season. They also have just five quarterback hits over the first two games.

Brian Burns' ankle injury doesn't exactly help, even though he wasn't producing like last season so far in 2026. New York will need Kayvon Thibodeaux to step up in Burns' absence. They may also look to employ rookie LB Arvell Reese more as a pass rusher, as he has been struggling in coverage.

item.title: He conned Travis Kelce, athletes and others out of millions. Who is Sid Jawahar?
item.description: Before Siddharth Jawahar was sentenced to prison this month and ordered to pay back $31 million to victims, he ran a Ponzi scheme for almost a decade.
item.content:encoded:
On Sept. 15, a federal judge in Missouri sentenced Siddharth Jawahar to 11 years in prison for using his Texas-based investment company to run a Ponzi scheme that swindled millions of dollars from investors including Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce.

Kelce was named as one of 64 victims in court by prosecutors during Jawahar's sentencing hearing, as first reported by a KMOV St. Louis reporter who was in the room and later confirmed by USA TODAY Sports, which obtained a court transcript of the hearing. It is not known how much money Kelce lost to the scheme. Along with Kelce, several NBA players were listed as investors in Jawahar's Swiftarc fund in a 2021 Forbes article.

Jawahar declined to be interviewed by USA TODAY Sports for this story but provided a comment through his attorney, Doug Passon.

"My client is ultimately responsible for making Travis Kelce a victim of fraud," Passon wrote in an email. "But the government has re-victimized Mr. Kelce by unnecessarily invoking his name at sentencing, which is the direct cause of this media frenzy. For an entity that purports to respect the rights of victims, the choice made by AUSA Derek Wiseman is difficult to understand."

Detroit Pistons guard Gary Harris Jr. and former NFL player Ross Travis (a close friend of Kelce) are plaintiffs in a separate federal civil lawsuit filed against Jawahar and obtained by USA TODAY Sports, in which Harris and Travis both allege that they invested money with and were defrauded by Jawahar.

Representatives for Kelce, Harris and Travis did not respond to messages from USA TODAY Sports seeking comment.

Before Jawahar's high-profile conviction, he rubbed elbows with professional athletes and a former U.S. president, and was involved in various philanthropic fundraisers – all while, prosecutors say, he was spending his investors' money on luxury hotels and private jets.

How did a 38-year-old venture capitalist from India orchestrate a multimillion-dollar Ponzi scheme that, over the course of almost a decade ensnared scores of people, including NFL and NBA players?

According to a federal indictment obtained by USA TODAY Sports, from about July 2016 through December 2023, Jawahar took in more than $35 million from Swiftarc investors but invested only about $10 million. He used to rest to pay off previous investors and fund "extravagant lifestyle expenses, including payments for flights on private planes, stays at luxury hotels, and expensive outings at lavish restaurants," the indictment said.

Jawahar pleaded guilty to three counts of wire fraud in January. On Sept. 15, he was ordered to pay a total of $31.35 million in restitution to "non-public victims."

At his sentencing hearing, Jawahar apologized to his victims and promised to pay restitution.

"The past two and a half years of my life have not been a joke," Jawahar said according to the court transcript. "I have looked at myself in the mirror, and I faced my darkest, deepest truths. It is not a coincidence that I have come to terms with them."

How Sid Jawahar orchestrated a Ponzi scheme

The Department of Justice described Jawahar as residing in the United States illegally, though it is unclear when he first arrived in the country.

The University of Texas at Austin has online records of a student named Siddharth Jawahar attending from fall 2005 to spring 2012, though there is no record of him earning a degree.

Jawahar, who sometimes signed his first name as "Sid" on official documents, first registered Swiftarc Capital LLC with the Texas Secretary of State in 2010 and listed a business address in Austin, according to state records. As recently as 2022, according to an annual franchise tax report, he listed his personal mailing address as an address belonging to the upscale Four Seasons Private Residences in downtown Austin.

Jawahar created Swiftarc Capital with another man, Siamc Kamalie, who was listed as the company's registered agent in Texas Secretary of State documents. On May 20, 2021, Kamalie resigned as Swiftarc Capital's registered agent but remained listed as a member/manager in the company's last public information report filed in October 2022. Kamalie, who has not been accused of wrongdoing and now works for Austin-based investment management firm Skycatcher, did not respond to a USA TODAY Sports message seeking comment for this story.

By 2015, according to court documents, Jawahar began investing the majority of his clients' money into a single overseas company, Philip Morris Pakistan. When that company's value fell, Jawahar covered up the losses and claimed to his clients that they were making profits. He continued to solicit funds from new investors to pay off his earlier investors.

As part of the alleged scheme, Jawahar also operated several other related business entities based in Texas, Florida and Ohio.

'My biggest loss ... is my reputation'

In 2019, Jawahar co-founded venture capital firm Swiftarc Ventures with Norwood Investments CEO Frank Krasovec and angel investor Zohar Ziv, according to an executive overview of the company filed as evidence in court. The firm's main growth equity fund touted investments in Uber, Domino's China, Planet Fitness and more.

In June 2022, state records show that the Texas State Securities Board sent Jawahar a cease and desist notice warning him to stop "engaging in fraud" and revoked Swiftarc Capital's authority to conduct investment activities. But Jawahar did not tell his investors about the disciplinary order and continued to take their money until he was arrested in early 2024, according to the indictment.

Kravosec and Ziv, the Swiftarc Ventures co-founders, say they were victimized by Jawahar's scam and are now suing Jawahar in civil court. On Sept. 15, Kravosec spoke at Jawahar's sentencing hearing and urged the judge to impose a maximum sentence.

"My biggest loss – forget my financial loss – is my reputation," Kravosec said, according to a court transcript. "That's all I have. You can't buy it. It's priceless. I feel that my reputation has been tainted along with others. And for that, I recommend the maximum sentence you can provide, Your Honor."

After Jawahar's indictment, the Department of Justice said that, "Jawahar tried to obstruct justice by trying to coach a victim into giving a favorable statement to the FBI, lying about his immigration status and finances and trying to get his sister to remotely wipe his iPhone to hide evidence."

Before his sentencing, Jawahar agreed to pay $10,000 to hire Jeff Roe, the founder of Republican political consulting firm Axiom Strategies, to secure favorable media coverage and letters of support to influence the judge. Prosecutors obtained a recorded jail call from Aug. 31 in which Jawahar asked Roe about a Jefferson City News Tribune article published two days earlier and asked about the consultant's progress in getting a politician to vouch for him.

Three days after the recorded jail call, on Sept. 3, Missouri congressman Sam Graves sent a letter to the judge urging him to impose a four-year prison sentence for Jawahar. Roe worked as Graves' chief of staff from 2001-2005, according to his LinkedIn profile. Roe and Graves did not respond to requests for comment.

Jawahar later swore in court that he never actually paid Roe. In an email to USA TODAY Sports, Passon described the Roe arrangement as "noise" and objected to the government slinging "mud" at sentencing.

"Sid Jawahar is a very good man, who has made some very serious mistakes and is taking ownership of all of it," Passon said in a statement to USA TODAY Sports. "He has made every effort from a jail cell in St. Genevieve to recoup restitution for victims and plans to continue to do. His efforts at helping other inmates improve their lives at St. Genevieve speak the loudest about his true character and heart for service. He is, like all of us, more than our worst mistakes.”

Sid Jawahar's known associates

Although the full list of people victimized by Jawahar's scheme is not public, he has ties to many famous figures in sports and politics.

Posts on Jawahar's public X account show him posing alongside President Bill Clinton, former tennis star Andy Roddick and NFL player turned television host Michael Strahan.

Tax return filings for the nonprofit Andy Roddick Foundation, which is based in Austin, list Jawahar as a board member for the organization from 2017 through 2019. A foundation representative did not respond to a USA TODAY Sports email inquiring about Jawahar's role.

According to a 2021 Forbes article, professional athletes who invested in Swiftarc include Kelce, Harris, Miami Heat guard Tim Hardaway Jr. and NBA free agent center Mason Plumlee. It is unclear if Hardaway or Plumlee were victims of Jawahar's fraud, and neither responded to USA TODAY Sports' attempts to reach them.

In a 2024 complaint filed in U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Ohio, Harris and Travis – a former Kansas City Chiefs teammate of Kelce's who last played in the NFL in 2021 – describe being defrauded by Jawahar. According to the lawsuit, Harris invested a total of $300,000 in one of Jawahar's funds based on Swiftarc's promised partnership with product innovation firm Nottingham Spirk, but the partnership never happened.

Harris eventually received $125,000 back after making numerous demands, while Travis invested $12,000 into the same fund and never received any return, the complaint said.

The Forbes article described Jawahar as having a "strong relationship" with Harris, who was quoted as saying, "Being around Sid has helped me grow so much as a person, especially looking to do more things than just basketball.”

The article also quoted Jawahar as saying, “For a lot of people, (venture capital) is something they have in their portfolio and they're wealthy enough to where it may or may not matter. But regardless of how important it is from a wealth component, I feel like Gary makes an effort to read all the quarterly updates, ask questions about them and be as engaged as one could ask for."

The Forbes article said Swiftarc had raised about $25 million at the time and was targeting investments in roughly a dozen consumer technology and health and wellness companies.

Jawahar has admitted to stealing money from investors, but why he did it remains a mystery.

At Jawahar's Sept. 15 sentencing hearing, FBI agent Craig Snider testified that he interviewed Jawahar in 2024. When asked why he perpetuated the fraud scheme, according to Snider, Jawahar, "said his motivation was greed, and any other adjective would be incorrect."

Jawahar's attorney, Passon, described his client in court as a man who lost his way while striving for success.

"He built this lifestyle for himself, from a boy in India to a student in UT, all the way in America, to all the reputation," Passon said, per the court transcript. "Not because he is a fraudster. Not because he is greedy. It's because he was hungry to make a life for himself. He was hungry for success. And success brings material trappings."

When Jawahar himself spoke at the hearing, with his mother, sister and fiancée in the courtroom, he said he took full responsibility for his actions but simultaneously blamed his own "deeply rooted traumas."

"My moral compass was misguided," Jawahar said, according to the court transcript. "Things happened in my childhood that I was not able to deal with in an adult fashion. I tried to outperform to run away from those fears. I drank too much. I put on these false guises of success, while the real issues were within me from my past."

He continued, "I learned also, Your Honor, that in order to heal a hurt, you have to feel a wound. And I realize that my ghosts are mine, and I have to encounter them in earnest and in honesty and truth. And I have begun that journey."

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: He conned Travis Kelce, athletes and others out of millions. Who is Sid Jawahar?

item.title: 5 Questions with the Enemy: Asking a Broncos fan how the Rams should attack Vance Joseph’s defense
item.description: “Even dating back to the playoffs last year, the Broncos struggled to stop the run" says Mile High Report
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Rams look to continue building momentum as they hit the road again, this time against the Denver Broncos on Sunday night. According to FanDuel Sportsbook, the Rams are a 2.5-point favorite in the Mile High City against the reigning AFC runner-up.

Including the playoffs, the Broncos have gone 26-13 under veteran head coach Sean Payton. Denver, like LA, is a Super Bowl hopeful. Ahead of this weekend’s primetime showdown, I spoke with Ian St. Clair of Mile High Report to get more intel on the Broncos.

Q – The Broncos have struggled mightily on offense in the first two games. Denver scored 10 points against the Chiefs in Week 1 and started slowly versus the Jaguars before scoring 17 unanswered points to secure the win. What is your initial impression of offensive coordinator Davis Webb, and what areas must the unit improve on moving forward?

A – Through the first six quarters, Bo Nix and the offense did struggle. However, it finally clicked in the second half. “Finally,” like it’s been half of the season. But what the Broncos offense showed against a good team and defense is an appetizer of what the unit can become. If Denver converts the two first-half trips to the red zone into touchdowns, the discussion changes. That’s where the focus should be – on finishing drives. That also takes care of the other issue – starting faster offensively. Dating back to last season, the Broncos offense doesn’t get going until the second half. That must change, and finishing drives is the first step. Denver also must stick with the running game. We saw it in the second half against the Jaguars, but consistently and effectively running the ball sets up the rest of the offense. 

As for Webb, he got into a rhythm in the second half and called a great game. Take that to Sunday night, build off it, and find ways to improve the offense even more. Webb is a bright young mind and he had some struggles to start. Some of it was execution, but just like life, he’ll need to take the failures and successes together. He has another big test this Sunday.  

Q – Speaking of offense, new wide receiver Jaylen Waddle had a great game against Jacksonville, catching eight passes for 138 yards. How are you enjoying the Waddle-Bo Nix connection two games in?

A – What will make me enjoy it even more is if that type of playmaking becomes consistent, thus making the offense harder to defend. It’ll force defenses to shift coverages to ensure Waddle is the focal point. That then opens the ability to utilize Courtland Sutton, Marvin Mims (when healthy), Pat Bryant, Troy Franklin and Evan Engram. After Sunday, I’m enjoying the Nix-Waddle connection quite a bit, but I want to see how Denver expands it. 

Q – The Broncos have had one of the NFL’s best defenses in the last two seasons under defensive coordinator Vance Joseph. If you’re Sean McVay, what types of plays should you be calling to keep Joseph’s unit on its toes on Sunday night? 

A – Test the Denver rush defense. Even dating back to the playoffs last year, the Broncos struggled to stop the run. The biggest issue against Kenneth Walker III and the Chiefs is that Denver couldn’t tackle. The tackling was much better for the Broncos against Jacksonville, but run Kyren Williams and Blake Corum on Sunday night. That allows McVay to use the heavy offensive sets that he typically likes to run, especially the plays with three tight ends. Then he can have Matthew Stafford use those tight ends in the passing game. That’s the other thing Denver struggles with – covering tight ends. Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad, in a word, are not very good. So force the two linebackers into coverage and the Rams will likely have success.

Q – Denver advanced to the AFC Championship last season and likely would’ve advanced to the Super Bowl had Nix stayed healthy. The team has certainly come a long way from the Nathaniel Hackett and Russell Wilson days, so what are your realistic expectations for the Broncos this season?

A – Payton, Nix and this Denver team should compete for the Super Bowl again. To be honest, this could be the Super Bowl matchup. It is just Week 3, but these two teams could meet again on Valentine’s Day in LA. And both teams have that expectation. There’s no doubt the opener on Monday Night Football in KC was startling, but similar to the Rams, the Broncos struggle in September. The team we saw in Denver in the second half against a good Jaguars team is the team that will make it a contender. 

Q – What is one question that you have for Rams fans?

A – How do fans feel about the “Super Team” moniker and all that comes with it?

item.title: By the Numbers: Saints vs. Raiders
item.description: Previewing the New Orleans Saints and Las Vegas Raiders Week 3 matchup
item.content:encoded:
Both the New Orleans Saints and Las Vegas Raiders are coming off road victories ahead of their week three matchup in the Big Easy. Las Vegas defeated the Los Angeles Chargers 26-14 for their second win in as many weeks, while New Orleans upset the Baltimore Ravens 24-17, picking up their first win and improving to 1-1. Let’s check out the breakdown of numbers for this week’s contest.

8: Las Vegas is tied for 1st in the NFL with eight sacks as a team through two games. The Raiders already have five players with at least one sack, so you never know who will wind up getting after the QB. This could be bad news for a Saints team with a struggling offensive line that has already given up eight sacks this year and will now be without starting LT Kelvin Banks Jr. for an extended period after landing on IR with a high ankle sprain.

35: Las Vegas’ fifth-round selection CB Hezekiah Masses, who rocks jersey number 35, has looked every bit the part of an NFL talent through the Raiders’ first two games. The rookie from California (Cal) is already making his mark in the defensive backfield with two interceptions (tied 1st in the league) and three passes defensed (tied 7th in the league).

55.6: Kirk Cousins has faced the New Orleans Saints nine times in his career and has a near even split of 5-4 in those games, or a .556 record. Most recently, Cousins swept the division series in 2025 against New Orleans as a member of the Atlanta Falcons, but the veteran QB will now return to the Superdome at the helm of Klint Kubiak’s offense with the Raiders.

60: New Orleans is celebrating its 60th season as an NFL franchise this year, and Sunday will mark the home opener inside the Caesars Superdome for the celebratory year.

136.5: After facing two of the top running backs in the NFL in Jahmyr Gibbs and Derrick Henry, the Saints have given up an average of 136.5 yards on the ground per game. Things will not get much easier for New Orleans as they will now hope to slow down agile RB Ashton Jeanty whose managed 210 all-purpose yards thus far.

662: The Saints have found themselves a QB of the future (and current) in Louisville product Tyler Shough. The second-year QB currently has a league-leading 662 passing yards and will now attempt to throw the first TD pass against the Raiders’ defense this season.

2021: The Raiders have not begun a season with a 3-0 record since 2021. Las Vegas, then led by QB Derek Carr, had two overtime victories in the first three weeks of the regular season. This is also the last time that the team made the postseason.

2023: Meanwhile, New Orleans has not gotten out of September with a winning record since 2023, when they beat the Tennessee Titans and Carolina Panthers to open the season. Sunday’s game will have a huge effect on the trajectory of the rest of both squads’ seasons.

item.title: The under-looked cause to the Ravens’ 1-1 start
item.description: The hidden culprit sabotaging the Ravens
item.content:encoded:
Much has been made of yet another Ravens’ fourth quarter collapse during their loss to the Saints in Week 2. “It was the defense’s fault!” or “it was Declan Doyle’s fault!” have been reccuring phrases from fans. While we are all quick to scapegoat, there is actually a much simpler issue that, if fixed, would have the Ravens sitting at the top of the NFL standings — penalties. Not just any type of penalties, though, but specifically ones that absolutely kill drives and positive plays. 

Through two weeks, the Ravens have lost -11.0 EPA on the penalties themselves, second-most in the NFL behind only the Carolin Panthers. That number undersells the damage, though. It only captures what happened on the flag, not what the flag took away.

Add in the value of the plays those penalties erased and the picture gets worse. The Ravens’ nullified plays were worth a combined +9.2 EPA, by far the most in the league. Baltimore isn’t getting flagged for holding on a stuffed run or an incomplete pass. It’s having productive plays called back again and again: a Ja’Kobi Lane touchdown, a 19-yard catch by Rashod Bateman, an 11-yard grab by Mark Andrews, a Lamar Jackson first down scramble. Combine the two, and the Ravens’ total penalty cost comes to -20.1 EPA, just a hair behind Carolina’s -20.2.

Unfortunately, there’s more . . . most offenses make back some of what they lose by drawing flags from opposing defenses. The Panthers have recovered +3.1 EPA that way, and Minnesota and Buffalo have each gained more than +19. Baltimore has gained, drum roll . . . zero. The Ravens are the only offense in the league without a single accepted defensive penalty.

That leaves Baltimore with a net offensive penalty EPA of -20.1, the worst mark in the NFL. No team has lost more to penalties on offense, and no team has gotten less back.


Then, you factor in some of the questionable calls at the end of the Saints game – that’s really when I started scratching my head. Is it possible that the Ravens are only committing offensive penalties on very successful plays, and the opposing defense hasn’t committed a penalty? 

A number of the team’s offensive penalties have certainly been valid but there are some that haven’t been. Chris Moore’s holding penalty last week and John Simpson’s “chop block” in Week 1 were highly questionable. The opposing team hasn’t been the victim of any of these 50/50 calls — especially on plays that yield very positive results. Obviously, you would surmise that these penalties are in-part leading to some of these eventually negated plays, but the Ravens have also generated explosive plays without them, so that doesn’t seem valid. 


These penalties had a major swing factor against the Saints, especially the ones in the 3rd quarter, which led to them losing ~5 expected points. The Ravens had reached the Saints 28 yard line, but were backed all the way up by penalties, resulting in a field goal. They were moving the ball effortlessly and would have probably scored a touchdown. For some quick back of hand math, the Ravens lost by seven points. If those flags did not occur, they should have theoretically been in position to win or tie the game at the end with a field goal – at the very least.

Obviously, none of this really matters now and the result is the result. However, the Ravens clearly need to clean up this penalty mess. It’s costing them big time and while part of this is on the Ravens technique, you would clearly expect some of the penalty luck to naturally start swinging in their favor soon. Two weeks isn’t a large sample size but at this pace, they are on track to shatter the NFL record for the most net expected points lost to penalties on offense.

What does all this mean? Yes, the Ravens need to clean some things up – but I have a feeling some good luck might be coming their way. They are currently on pace to quadruple the NFL record for net penalty EPA lost on offense, and that probably won’t continue.

item.title: Giants vs. Titans: How will New York handle Brian Daboll’s offense?
item.description: Can the Giants bounce back in Week 3 against the Titans?
item.content:encoded:
The New York Giants are regrouping for a Week 3 matchup against the 0-2 Tennessee Titans. New York lost starting quarterback Jaxson Dart for the season, a brutal gut-punch. The Giants are 2.5-point favorites, with the Over/Under at 39.5 points.

The Giants welcome back former head coach Brian Daboll. It is the Titans’ first road game of the 2026 season. Tennessee is rebuilding in Robert Saleh’s first season as head coach, but does have its quarterback of the foreseeable future and a few young offensive weapons.

Let’s look at how the Giants’ defense matches up with Tennessee’s offense.

Brian Daboll’s offense

Daboll took Carmen Bricillo, Shea Tierney, and Cade Knox to Nashville to coach under Saleh. Daboll inherited quarterback Cam Ward, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. Ward looked much more comfortable in the Titans’ 24-20 last-second loss against the Philadelphia Eagles. Daboll’s squad mustered only 10 points in their Week 1 loss to the Jets.

The Titans have used 11 personnel at a 71% rate through two games — as expected after signing Wan’Dale Robinson to a four-year, $70-million contract. Ward has operated under center at a 37% rate; under Daboll last season, Dart was under center only 20% of the time.

The Titans’ offense has yet to eclipse 300 yards in a game this season. They’re 10 of 25 on third down (40% conversion rate), and they have three touchdowns through two games; Ward has two touchdowns on the ground, and he threw a touchdown pass to Elic Ayomanor in Week 1. Ayomanor dropped a touchdown in Week 2, but the throw was off-target.

Ward is 32 of 53 (61.5%) through the air for 323 yards (6.2 YPA) with just one touchdown and no interceptions. Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears split rushing work, but rookie Nicholas Singleton dressed after being a healthy scratch in Week 1.

Pollard has rushed 21 times for 99 yards (4.7 YPC) with six missed tackles forced and a 3.05 yards-after-contact number, while catching two passes for zero yards. Spears sprung a long catch in Week 2 and has secured four passes for 41 yards through two games. He averaged 5.3 yards per carry with just ten rushes for 53 yards, and an impressive 3.90 yards after contact.

Tennessee’s receiving corps consists of three young receivers: Ayomanor, Chimere Dike, and first-round pick Carnell Tate. Robinson operates the slot, and Calvin Ridley is still a Titan. Ridley has played 62% of the snaps this season. Tennessee used more 12 personnel against the Eagles, leading to more Daniel Bellinger, who is the second tight end behind Gunnar Helm.

Ayomanor leads the Titans in receiving yards; he’s caught three of six targets for 80 yards and one receiving touchdown. Tate has seen 11 targets and secured seven for 65 yards. Robinson has caught six of seven for 47 yards, and Helm has secured all six of his targets for 41 yards.

The Titans’ offensive line has former Giants’ center Austin Schlottmann anchoring the unit; Pro Football Focus has graded him well in pass protection, but poorly in run blocking, which is consistent across the Titans’ front, who dealt with two solid defensive fronts with the Eagles and Jets.

Dan Moore Jr. and JC Latham will have their hands full with the dangerous Giants’ pass rush on the edges, while Peter Skoronski and Fernando Carmona — the latter has surrendered four pressures on the season already — will be starting at guard for Bricillo. The Giants can win the matchup of the trenches.

Giants’ game plan

Dart wasn’t the only significant loss in Week 2. Brian Burns had his ankle rolled up on with six minutes left in the 28-6 game. The Giants will be without their star edge defender, which will force Dennard Wilson to change how he uses his personnel.

Kayvon Thibodeaux is in for an increased role without Burns. He’s played 59 snaps so far this season to Burns’ 91 and Abdul Carter’s 108. Chauncey Golston may receive more snaps on the edge, as well as Arvell Reese in certain packages.

Tae Banks remains questionable for the game; if he can not dress, Colton Hood will receive the spot opposite Greg Newsome II. The Giants should dress Jason Pinnock in this game as insurance behind Tyler Nubin, who was attacked by McVay’s offense in Week 2.

The Giants faced a Rams team that used 13 personnel on over half of their snaps — that won’t be the case against Brian Daboll’s offense. Giants’ nickel cornerback, Dru Phillips, played on just 48% of snaps against the Rams, after playing on in 83% against Dallas. Expect to see less base personnel and more nickel packages against a Titans team that has run 11 personnel at a 71% rate. Daboll has used 12 personnel at an 18% rate.

The 17% blitz rate from Week 2 is going to increase in Week 3. Cam Ward has been blitzed at a 31% rate overall and a 38% rate on third down. I expect to see more five-man rushes from the Giants. Wilson should dictate via aggression against the young quarterback.

There is an option to expand Reese’s role as a blitzer, too. Reese has 11 pass rush snaps this season; possible use of him on the edge in certain situations versus 11 personnel could be something for the Giants to explore. New York could use a lot of Cover-3, middle-of-the-field-closed with both strong/weak-side buzz rotation against 3×1 sets.

Final thoughts

I expect the Giants, although injured, will handle business against the Titans. I believe we’ve seen the worst of Jameis Winston, and he’ll help stabilize the offense, which will likely be in 12 and 22 personnel often. I also expect Wilson to have more freedom and comfort to get creative against Ward and Daboll’s offense. I have the Giants winning, 20-13.

item.title: Cowboys roundtable discussion: BrandonAubrey, Jaishawn Barham, and Brazil
item.description: Here is our latest roundtable with a panel of BTB writers giving us their answers to this week’s questions
item.content:encoded:
Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo, Dyllan Rivers, Tom Ryle and Sean Martin. 

Do you have better faith in Brandon Aubrey after punching all seven kicks for points against the Commanders, which included a 60-yard field goal?

Mike – Honestly, the faith in Brandon Aubrey was already high, but games like that only make it stronger. Going perfect on all seven scoring kicks, including a 60-yarder, is not normal, that’s a weapon. Aubrey gives Dallas something most teams do not have, the ability to turn stalled drives near midfield into points and change how the coaching staff thinks about field position. The bigger issue is not whether Cowboys fans should trust Aubrey, it is whether the offense becomes too comfortable settling for him. 

Jorge – I think he calmed some of the nerves, for sure. He needed, and the fans needed, to see that 60-yarder go through, and he nailed it. As long as he doesn’t have a Brett Maher-like meltdown, he should still be considered among the best kickers in the NFL and a huge asset for this team.

Tom – All he can do to calm our doubts is to nail his kicks, and he did. I feel pretty good about him going forward.

Sean – He’s butter. What else is there to say? The kicks sure looked good to me.

Dyllan – I was only about 3.6% worried after last week. Now I’m back to a solid 0.0% in the worried about Aubrey department. Butter is simply the best there is.

What grade do you give Jaishawn Barham for his first game wearing the green-dot, and where does he need improvement?

Mike – I’d give Barham a B+ for his first game wearing the green dot. For a young linebacker taking on that much responsibility, he looked ready for the moment. The forced fumble was the headline, but the bigger takeaway was that the defense did not look utterly overwhelmed with him communicating calls and helping get players aligned. The improvement still needs to come but it was a quality start. 

Jorge – If we’re going with a letter grade, I’d have to say he was a B. Some of the communication issues were cleaned up, but the defense still had issues and gave up some plays, particularly in containment of Jayden Daniels, who ran wild at times. Still, Dallas is asking a ton out of the rookie, and the defense’s slight improvement is a good sign. Barham was a big part of that improvement, and one would think he’s only going to get better. 

Tom – B sounds about right. That was a huge load to put on the rookie’s shoulders, and he bore it well. And he caused one of the biggest plays of the game, and the best highlight for the defense so far this year.

Sean – I’ll go with a B as well. We want to have higher expectations for this defense, and then they go and start an unproven rookie day two pick smack dab in the middle of the defense, and it makes those expectations difficult. Like Jorge said it wasn’t perfect, but the Dallas defense put tangible things to build off on on tape with some of their alignments, coverages, hustle to the ball, and of course a takeaway which was caused directly by Barham lowering the “Bar-hammer”. 

Dyllan – I’ll give Barhammer a B+ this week. The defense looked much tighter in communication with the rookie LB wearing the green dot. He also made some great plays throughout, including the forced fumble to put the offense in great field position. He somehow morphs through blocks and is always around the ball. This kid is going to be special.

This week sees the Cowboys travelling to Brazil to face the Baltimore Ravens. Their last international game was in London back in 2014 with a 31-14 victory, but how confident are you feeling for this international clash?

Mike – Cautiously confident is how I put it, and I’ve seen first hand how the Cowboys handle international pressure watching them in London way back when. The Cowboys have momentum after the Washington win, and an international stage should not scare a franchise that has handled this kind of spotlight before. The concern is the opponent. Baltimore brings the type of physical, awkward matchup that can expose any lack of discipline, especially with the travel, different routine, and field-condition questions in Brazil.

Jorge – I am worried. It’s a 10-plus-hour flight, over 4,000 miles across three time zones, to a country in spring while we’re in fall, which could affect the natural circadian rhythm, and that’s a big deal. As someone who has traveled from Japan to the U.S. several times, that is not a trip to take lightly. On top of that, the Ravens are coming off a tough loss against the Saints and are going to be locked in for the bounce-back win, and oh, by the way, they own us historically in the head-to-head matchup six wins to one. My worry scale would be at a 9 out of 10 in this case.

Tom – I’m not too worried about that rhythm, because the day will be almost exactly the same length. What does worry me is that Dallas has been so vulnerable to running quarterbacks. Now here comes Lamar Jackson. If they can’t find a way to slow him down on the ground, this one will be rough. Oh, and the pass defense hasn’t exactly sparkled so far. The early spread had the Cowboys as a three point underdog, and I think that is a bit kind to them. I have some hope if the offense can continue to ball out, but that may be a tall order against Baltimore.

Sean – The pregame thoughts on this game feel too chalk, as if something completely unexpected is going to happen. The Ravens seem to have this type of early season head-scratching loss where they implode every single year, and the Cowboys have a win that still leaves an uneasy feeling. Logic would say keep going down the chalk line and the Ravens own the Cowboys yet again. My worry about that being a possibility in Brazil is still at a firm 7/10, but things are rarely, rarely this easy to predict in pro football, so let’s just see what Rio de Janeiro has in store.

Dyllan – I’m extremely worried. Dallas has struggled against two mobile QBs through the first two weeks. Now they have the opportunity to face the best mobile quarterback in the NFL. On top of that, the ageless wonder Derrick Henry adds an intensity that not many other backs possess. Mix in the traveling and the beat up field; this is going to be a sloppy, brutal game for both sides.

RAPID FIRE 

Who scores first for Dallas?

Jorge – CeeDee Lamb stays hot.

Tom – I’m going to stick with Javonte Williams.

Sean – Hunter Luepke. You gotta get weird for an international game.

Dyllan – George Pickens gets the first TD of the game and his first TD of the season. 

Jake Ferguson receptions- 4.5,  over or under?

Jorge – Under; Ferg is still too erratic for me to buy consecutive weeks of big impact like 5 receptions. 

Tom – Under. I’d guess George Pickens is going to get a lot of balls.

Sean – I’ll go over.

Dyllan – Under. Dallas just has so many weapons.

Javonte Williams rushing yards- 59.5, over or under?

Jorge – Under; Ravens currently own the 6th-best run defense in the NFL, and the Cowboys are struggling to get the ground game going. 

Tom – Under. Same reasons.

Sean – Under this time.

Dyllan – Under. Dallas has struggled to run the ball. I don’t see that changing now.

Lamar Jackson rushing yards- 59.5, over or under?

Jorge – Over; Jayden Daniels just ran for 69 yards in one half. Lamar is going to feast. 

Tom – Unfortunately, over. The defense is helpless against running QBs.

Sean – Under because he still wants to throw the ball first.

Dyllan – Over. Dallas has struggled vs mobile QBs and now they face the king of mobile QBs.

Sacks recorded by Dallas- 1.5, over or under?

Jorge – Under; Although the Cowboys’ pressure looked good at times, they didn’t register a single sack against Daniels or Mariota, and they have been poor tacklers in the first two games. 

Tom – Under, sadly.

Sean – Yeah, under.

Dyllan – Under. Although I think the chopped field may play a role in helping them in this department.

Brandon Aubrey field goals made-2.5, over or under?

Jorge – Over; These international games become a struggle, and I imagine the Cowboys’ offense will cool off a bit, and Aubrey will be called upon frequently. 

Tom – Over. I see the offense stalling against the Ravens D.

Sean – Over too.

Dyllan – Not sure if the field conditions allow for super long kicks, but we’ll go with the over here.

item.title: Broncos vs Rams 5 questions: What does Aaron Donald’s return mean?
item.description: The Rams got one of the best defensive lineman back in Donald. Now LA looks to get their first road win on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Donald is back.

Unfortunately, or fortunately for the Denver Broncos, Myles Garrett is on IR. But bringing back one of the best defensive linemen in NFL history to a defense is obviously huge.

That’s one of the reasons the Los Angeles Rams were heavy favorites to win the Super Bowl heading into the season and still are the favorites. Offensively, LA has the reigning MVP and an explosive offense. So what does the return of Donald mean?

To get a feel for the Rams and how big it was to get their first win against the New York Giants, we go “behind enemy lines” with Evan Craig from Turf Show Times.

MHR: How important was that win over the New York Giants on Monday night? What was different between the first two games

Evan: The win was extremely important and exactly what the doctor ordered. Los Angeles looked all out of sorts in Week 1, and the 49ers took full advantage. New York really didn’t stand a chance, even if Jaxson Dart had never gotten injured. The Rams poured too many resources into improving this offseason, and they weren’t about to let the Giants ruin that by dropping them to 0-2. I will say, there are things to clean up, especially as LA was only up 11 at halftime. It should’ve been much worse, but back-to-back turnovers on a Matthew Stafford pick and a signature Kyren Williams fumble momentarily gave the G-Men hope. 

Still, it was a night-and-day difference. It helped that the Rams, as Sean McVay eloquently put it, didn’t have a “dumbass” travel plan ahead of the game. Much of their awful showing in Australia was due to the fact that they arrived a day before the game. Several new pieces needed to gel together, but it was mainly due to the travel plan

MHR: What does the return of Aaron Donald mean for the Rams defense and the team?

Evan: Aaron Donald’s return means a great deal to this team, and Monday night was a huge reminder of why. 

During the win over the Giants, AD didn’t put together much of a stat line, yet his presence was felt on every one of his 33 snaps. It was also as if he had never left, with his power and burst on full display. That was impressive to see in someone who was two years removed from the game. I guess that fitness regimen he was on during retirement certainly paid off. If he gets better as the season progresses, and it’s very likely he does, that should scare all opposing offensive coordinators. Now, imagine what will happen once Myles Garrett returns. Did anyone else get chills?

At first, Donald’s return seemed like nothing more than a gimmick and an unnecessary distraction for a team aiming for another Super Bowl run. Gimmick might not be the correct word, as he seemed genuine about returning, even if a large percentage of the NFL world was doubting it. Clearly, Rams fans can see he’s committed to helping the team secure a ring. Maybe you can go home after all.

MHR: How does LA get the win on Sunday night? What must the Rams do defensively and offensively?

Evan: LA will get the win if they take a page out of the Chiefs’ Week 1 playbook. Kansas City rushed for 220 yards and ran the ball down the Broncos’ throats in the opener. Against the Giants, the Rams’ two-headed attack of Williams and Blake Corum combined for 164 rushing yards. They have a strong enough attack on the ground to keep Denver on its toes all game. Also, the Rams must have better pass distribution. Davante Adams and Terrance Ferguson combined for 19 targets when no other pass catcher had more than two targets. Spreading the ball out will help take the pressure off Adams, especially if Puka Nacua’s out. The Rams have a diverse array of playmakers to make this happen. 

Defensively, the Rams must make the Broncos one-dimensional. Denver doesn’t have the strongest running game, but if LA can take away that run game and put a ton of pressure on Bo Nix, they can secure the win. Nix is a very capable quarterback, yet assuming the Rams follow KC’s playbook, they can limit his effectiveness by taking away his new favorite target in Jaylen Waddle and security blankets Courtland Sutton and Troy Franklin.

MHR: What do you make of the current spread? And what is your best bet for the game?

Evan: I think 2.5 points is a fair spread, but I don’t like LA as the favorite. Denver is a really tough place to play, and the Broncos deserve more credit as a team, even if they haven’t had the smoothest start to begin the season. Yes, I believe the Rams are a better team on paper when they’re at full strength, yet they’re without Garrett and possibly Puka for this one. That, to me, feels like the sportsbooks are disrespecting Denver, at least this week, which wouldn’t be the first time for them. 

My best bet is Matthew Stafford under 200 passing yards. The Broncos have a far superior secondary than the Giants, meaning they won’t allow Davante Adams to run wild on them if, again, Nacua is out again this week. 

MHR: How does this game unfold, and what is your prediction?

Evan: This is a tough game to predict, since the Rams are typically slow starters to begin the season. Last season was their best start in years, and it was only with a 3-2 record. The Broncos were in the same boat in 2025 because they began the year 1-2 before winning 13 of their next 14 games to finish the season and clinch the top seed. That said, I wouldn’t be surprised if the Rams drop this one, which would certainly spell trouble among the fan base right before they travel to Philly. I also expect this to be a low-scoring game due to the strength of both defenses. The first one to 20 should win this one, and I expect it to be Denver. 

Broncos 21, Rams 17

item.title: Chiefs pass rush must improve after quiet Colts game
item.description: What should we make of two very different performances by the Kansas City defensive line?
item.content:encoded:
A pair of seemingly contradictory defensive performances for the Kansas City Chiefs have left fans pondering how much trust to put in the unit.

Kansas City opened the season with a dominant 31-10 beatdown of the Denver Broncos, sacking quarterback Bo Nix four times and holding the reigning AFC West champions to just 176 total yards.

A week later, however, the Chiefs sweated 70 full minutes for a 33-30 overtime victory over the Indianapolis Colts. The Colts gained 329 yards against Kansas City. Despite multiple close calls, quarterback Daniel Jones played five quarters without being sacked.

Speaking before Thursday’s practice, defensive line coach Joe Cullen credited the Indianapolis offensive line for thwarting the Chiefs’ pass rush.

“They’re a physical offensive line,” observed Cullen. “They’ve always had a good offensive line. And one of the things we stressed is we got to get them in those down and distances like we had a third-and-16. [Defensive end George Karlaftis] made a great play on the screen… We had a third-and-11, and George jumped the gun, went offside. So now you’re down to third-and-6, and the ball gets out a little quicker. But they’ve always had a decent offensive line. And I think we saved the best rush for the last one when George put him on his back, but they’re a good offensive line.”

On Thursday, defensive tackle Chris Jones reiterated the importance of wins and losses over all other stats while acknowledging the need for improvement. He does see an overtime victory as an indication of the Kansas City defense’s perseverance.

“I think the most important thing that matters is wins and losses,” said Jones. “We were able to pull through, but we were also able to learn a lot about this team — the resiliency of the team and the core strength of the team. But there are still areas for improvement.”

One area for improvement will be preventing quick passes — as Jones was able to seemingly get off for completions any time the Chiefs’ pass rush threatened him. Cullen knows it is a problem, but it will take the whole defense to prevent a repeat performance by opposing quarterbacks.

“We’ve had some consistent pressure,” remarked the coach, “and it’s not always going to be a sack, but we’ve put pressure on the quarterback in a lot of different ways. But the coverage in the back end and the rush go hand in hand. Those are the things that when they’re tied in together, you’ve got to get home. [When] the quarterback’s patting that ball for over three seconds, you’ve got to get home.

“Ball gets out quick —you may have to change your rush and get your hand up to knock a slant down. The slant’s getting out in 2.2 seconds. When you make the quarterback clutch it, you got to get home, and when he doesn’t, and he’s getting it out quick, we got to get our hands up and helping the slant game.”

The Chiefs’ defense will next be tested on Sunday in South Florida against the Miami Dolphins. Cullen expects a well-prepared squad from new head coach Jeff Hafley. The Chiefs also have respect for possibly the league’s fastest running back, De’Von Achane, and quarterback Malik Willis — who took Kansas City to overtime in 2022 while with the Tennessee Titans.

“We’re excited,” Cullen declared. “A great opportunity going on the road for the first time down to Miami, and Coach Hafley’s building that program, and they’ve got some really skilled athletes on offense. [Achane] — No. 28 —is as good a back as there is. He’s had 5.7 [yards] to carry last year. We played Malik Willis when he was at Tennessee in the game here. So great athletes, and we’ll have our hands full, but we’re excited and looking forward to the challenge.”

item.title: Bills trending up, trending down ahead of Week 3’s game vs. Chargers
item.description: Which Buffalo Bills are rising/falling with a Week 3 battle against the Los Angeles Chargers ahead?
item.content:encoded:
The Bills are 2-0 with the league’s top offense by DVOA. Facing a desperate Los Angeles Chargers team will offer a unique Week 3 test.

Justin Herbert has faced pressure on 45.5% of his dropbacks through two games, the second-highest rate in the league, and PFF has him at 28.7 when he’s under duress. The Chargers are 0-2, and their offense sits 27th in DVOA at -20.6%. The Bills sit second overall at 52.7%, with the league’s top offense at 56.8%, although the defense is 19th at +9.0%.

It’s a two-game sample, and the adjustments still lean on last season. Still, gives us an idea of where Sunday can be decided: can Buffalo’s defense get to Herbert before Herbert gets to it? Here are my choices for which Buffalo players could be decisive in next Sunday’s matchup.

HEROES

Greg Rousseau, OLB: the pass rush runs through him

Rousseau earned an 84.5 PFF grade against Houston and a 90.8 against Detroit, second among Bills defenders behind Deone Walker on Thursday. He has four sacks and three forced fumbles, including the strip-sack that closed out the Texans with 16 seconds left. He has looked like a natural fit at outside linebacker in Jim Leonhard’s defense, and I think the move was the best thing to happen to his production.

He lined up mostly over the right tackle in Week 1, which is Joe Alt this Sunday. I don’t expect him to simply beat Alt. Alt has a 75.3 PFF pass-block grade (23rd among tackles) with only two pressures allowed, and Bleacher Report ranked him the No. 2 right tackle in the league this summer. His weakness has been discipline: five penalties, four against the Raiders.

Rousseau will have a tougher test than the matchups he’s had so far. Hopefully, he can continue to impress and impact the game as he has done this season. Buffalo’s defense needs it.

Dion Dawkins, LT: the answer to Tuipulotu and Mack

Dawkins posted an 81.7 PFF grade against the Lions, fifth-best on the roster, and Bleacher Report graded him an A for a nearly perfect night against Aidan Hutchinson. In Week 1, he led the line with an 87.5% pass-block win rate in one-on-one situations, and Danielle Hunter had one of the quietest games of his career.

It wasn’t perfect, though. He whiffed on a key fourth-down block that day, and PFF had his run-blocking grade at 39.9. I think that matters, because the Chargers swallowed Ashton Jeanty last week, holding him to 2.4 yards per carry, for just 48 yards. However, we know the Shnowman can do his 1/11th in the run game, and the pass rush is where the challenge is bigger. Tuli Tuipulotu had 13 sacks and a 17.9% pressure rate last season, sixth in the league, and rookie Akheem Mesidor is the only Charger in the top 40 of PFF’s pass rush win rate at 20%. Against the Cardinals, Los Angeles produced just eight pressures, so the production hasn’t matched the names yet. Dawkins will decide whether that stays true on Sunday.

HEAD-SCRATCHERS

Christian Benford, CB: the best chance to get right

Benford was the third-lowest-graded Bill in Week 1 by PFF, and he has allowed 11 receptions, the most among corners before Monday night. That comes to roughly 118 yards and two touchdowns. He’s been beaten too often in man coverage for a number one corner who travels with the opponent’s WR1. Also, pairing a nice pass breakup with a pass interference in the end zone didn’t help.

To be fair, he drew Nico Collins and Amon-Ra St. Brown, and those two combined for 16 catches, 217 yards, and five touchdowns on 23 targets against the Bills’ defense as a whole, not against Benford alone. The Chargers offer a much easier week, at least on paper. Ladd McConkey is dealing with rib trouble and has eight catches, while every other Chargers wideout combined has the same number. If Benford stays home in coverage and doesn’t give Herbert clean throws, it’s a real chance he can start his comeback this season.

Landon Jackson, DE: I expected more

Jackson graded 33.1 in Week 1 and 36.1 in Week 2, the lowest on the roster against Detroit and a bottom-five grade both weeks. After a promising preseason, I expected him to make the most of the opportunity in TJ Sanders’ absence. So far, he has struggled with penalties and a lack of push, being almost invisible in the middle, and has allowed others like DeWayne Carter and Greg Gaines to outplay him.

The Chargers’ run game isn’t scary: Omarion Hampton had 43 yards on 12 carries in Week 1 and has fumbled in both games. It’s time for Jackson to start showing more, or he could be in danger of losing snaps to other teammates who have done better. The Bills can quietly get something from other guys inside, as Deone Walker starts to get all the attention from opposing offenses.

HONORABLE MENTIONS

Trending up

Deone Walker, DT:He was last week’s hero and is still climbing. Walker earned a 93.0 PFF grade, the best of any Bill against Detroit, with three quarterback hits and three batted balls, two of them on the same fourth-quarter drive. He has nine pressures and a sack on the season, per PFF, and the Chargers’ interior gives him a good target.

Keon Coleman, WR:He caught all six passes thrown to him against Detroit, with two third-down conversions on touchdown drives, and earned a 79.0 PFF grade. With DJ Moore’s shoulder in question, Coleman’s role matters more.(If his ankle allows him to play)

DeWayne Carter, DL:He earned a 75.5 PFF grade with Ed Oliver and T.J. Sanders inactive, and was very noticeable in his snps against the run.

Trending down

Spencer Brown, RT:Brown has been one of the best run-blocking tackles in football, ranking seventh in PFF’s run-block grade last season, and Bleacher Report placed him third among right tackles this summer. But his pass protection went the other way in 2025, dropping from 76.2 to 61.3 in PFF pass-block grade with 36 pressures allowed. Hutchinson beat him on the third play of Thursday’s game for a sack and forced fumble. With Khalil Mack coming to town, Brown will need to rebound this week.

Davison Igbinosun, CB:He has graded in the bottom five both weeks, at 41.2 and 38.8, though on limited snaps, and for a man corner, he’s been too grabby.

Final Thoughts

This defense is still a work in progress, but it isn’t as awful as some people believe, with a DVOA rank of 19th. Despite sitting at 0-2 now, the Chargers will be another good test for this unit, especially with Herbert being good from a clean pocket. The pass rush is the answer to that problem, and Rousseau and Walker are the ones producing it. Dawkins and Brown have to hold up on the other side to allow Josh Allen and the offense to continue to put up points on the board.

No matter if it’s Rousseau getting home or Benford keeping the receivers in front of him, the defense will have one job: hold the Chargers offense down, scoring less than the Bills. The players I mentioned today will be key, in my opinion. Let me know in the comments if you have more names to share.

Catch up on all this and more with the latest edition of Leading the Charge!

item.title: Five Good Texans Questions with Stampede Blue
item.description: Chris Sheperd of Stampede Blue joins BRB for five questions
item.content:encoded:
You stay in this game long enough and you start building relationships along the way. Chris Sheperd of Stampede Blue and I have been doing five questions for the last five years and it has been an enjoyable ride. Even though the Colts and Tecans are enemies on the field doesn’t mean we have to be enemies in the proverbial press box. Yet again, the Texans and Colts stand in each other’s way for playoff contention. Two 0-2 teams are coming off of two tough weeks and that is where our conversation began.

Battle Red Blog: Like the Texans, the Colts have started 0-2 but against quality opponents. Are you concerned or feel like the start is a function of the difficult competition?

Chris Shepard: Most Colts fans believe the sky is falling and given the history of the last decade they may be right to believe that. 

I am less concerned than most but concerned all the same. The defense went through a big turnover this offseason. Colts fans were largely over linebacker Zaire Franklin on and off of the field, but he was a long tenured leader of the defense as was corner Kenny Moore. Indy was right to move on from them in an attempt to do a soft reset on a leadership group that had yet to find sustained success. 

Just because it was the right thing to do doesn’t mean it’s going to yield immediate positive results. The Colts added a lot of young players and lower level free agents and so far we’ve seen them struggle to get to speed. Week two was a large improvement for the defense but I expect this defense won’t hit it’s stride until week 8 or 9, if they ever come together at all. 

Facing Lamar Jackson and Patrick Mahomes back to back against a young defense with so many new pieces was always going to be difficult and while I don’t think CJ Stroud is in that tier of quarterbacks, it’s not like things are going to be significantly easier for them in week three.

BRB: Injuries are a part of the game obviously. We all saw Alec Pierce leave the game on Sunday night. Are there any other injuries you are concerned about?

CS: Sauce Gardner went out in the second half with an injury, he was able to return but he was in obvious pain. Sauce has been very good through two weeks so I’ll be monitoring his progress throughout the week.

BRB: Who are some new faces we haven’t seen in this matchup that will play a key role on Sunday?

CS: Rookie safety AJ Halucy has gotten every opportunity to contribute so far thus season. Halucy, a third round pick out of LSU, hasn’t been bad but he has made some rookie mistakes. I suspect they’ll continue to give him the majority of the snaps at strong safety and there is plenty of reason to believe he’ll make more of an impact as the season goes on.

Rookie linebackers Bryce Boettcher (Oregon) and CJ Allen (Georgia) have been working their way into a linebacker rotation. Allen missed more than a month of training camp due to injury and is working his way back. Neither player has made much of an impact yet but week by week they should see more time on the field and week three should see another uptick of snaps for both.

BRB: This is an annual question. Who are you most concerned about in the AFC South and how do you see the division shaking out? Which divisional opponent do Colts fans enjoy beating the most?

CS: The Jaguars are my biggest concern followed closely by the Texans. Houston figured things out last season and while defensive success is more difficult to sustain year over year, DeMeco Ryans is a very good coach and I expect they’ll turn things around in short order. 

The Jaguars combination of Trevor Lawrence and Liam Coen has been solid. I’m less sold on Coen long term than I am on Ryans, I think that when things start to go bad for him he’s more likely to be unable to right the Jacksonville ship. But until that happens, the combo of Coen and Lawrence with that offense puts them at the top of the division.

Ultimately,  I think it’ll land on the Jaguars at the top and I hope Indy and Houston are in a battle for a wildcard spot headed into week 18 but given Houston’s recent history they absolutely have the advantage right now.

BRB: Fanduel has the Texans favored by 2.5. How do you see the game going on Sunday? Are there any other bets you feel comfortable recommending?

CS: I think that’s a fair line.Both teams are desperate and both are capable of winning. I see this one coming down to the wire, with both teams trading shots until the final moments.

In games like this one anything can happen and while I hope the Colts pull it off, Houston being the favorite makes sense.

We want to thank Chris for taking the time to answer our questions and for being such a joy to work with for all of these years. Remember, if you want to catch the best Colts coverage, please feel free to catch his site at Stampede Blue. We want to wish Chris the Colts the best of luck for the rest of the season. That is of course except for when they are playing the Texans.

item.title: Hunting Explosives: Revisiting the Bears’ Big Plays from Week 1
item.description: Breaking down the Chicago Bears' explosive plays highlighted by Caleb Williams, D’Andre Swift, and Kyle Monangai.
item.content:encoded:
Week 2 brought 8 more explosive plays. Wait – eight?! That can’t be right; let me go back and…yeah, eight. It’s honestly unbelievable the Chicago Bears didn’t win this one, but a fumble at the goal line and the Williams injury, combined with the constant rain, conspired to leave the Bears with only three points for their efforts. However, there was still some good stuff, particularly in the run game, as this 2026 Bears squad starts to figure out who they are going to be this year.

Explosive Play 2.1 – Q1 10:26, 2nd and 3 from the Chicago 38. Caleb Williams aborted snap, recovered at Chicago 36 by Williams, run up the middle for 17 yards.

Obviously an incredibly creative play call by Johnson to put the ball on the ground and just have Caleb run up the middle for an explosive play… Okay, maybe we should’ve known this one was going to be weird. Busted play, quarterback is talented enough to make it a chunk gain instead of a disaster.

Explosive Play 2.2 – Q3 14:50, 2nd and 10 from the Chicago 35. D’Andre Swift off left tackle for 12 yards.

The Bears come out in 12 personnel with Kmet attached on the right and Loveland attached on the left side of the line. Rome and Kalif Raymond line up stacked to the left of Loveland. At the snap, Raymond drags across to the right in what looks like a potential play action pass dump off option for a future play. Braxton and Loveland do enough to stalemate their defender and Thuney works up to the second level to get a hat on his assignment. Swift finds the space off the left tackle (hat tip to Rome for hanging with his defender) and with a little stutter step makes the safety miss in the hole, gaining another 6-7 before running out of bounds. Well blocked but Swift’s missed tackle takes it from a nice run to set up a third and short to a fresh set of downs.

Explosive Play 2.3 – Q3 14:10, 2nd and 10 from the Chicago 47. Caleb Williams scrambles up the middle for 11 yards.
